title: boundaryVanishing_finite (statement)
statement:
Let $\ell$ be prime, let $A$ be a finite commutative ring with $\ell^n\cdot1_A=0$ for some $n\in\mathbf N$, and let $k$ be a field of prime characteristic $p\ne\ell$ [def-weil-field]. Let $W$ and $\overline Y$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes and $r:W\to\overline Y$ a proper $k$-morphism [def-weil-finite-type-morphism; def-weil-proper-morphism]. Let $Z$ be any scheme and $c:Z\to\overline Y$ any morphism; no finiteness, separation, reducedness or immersion hypothesis is imposed on $Z$ or $c$. Put $T=W\times_{\overline Y}Z$, with projections $a:T\to W$ and $r_Z:T\to Z$ [def-pc-fibre-product].

Let $\Lambda$ be the sheafification of the constant ring presheaf with value $A$ on the profinite point [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring; def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], and put $\Lambda_S=p_S^*\Lambda$ on every scheme $S$ [sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Work in the ordinary unbounded derived categories of internal $\Lambda_S$-modules, with total derived pullback and pushforward [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull]. For every $K\in\Dctf(W,\Lambda)$ in the finite constant-local-model convention [det-def-sfb-constructible-tor-amplitude], assume also bounded constructibility in the general ring-object convention [sk-def-sfb-bounded-constructible]. Then
$$
La^*K\simeq0\quad\Longrightarrow\quad Lc^*Rr_*K\simeq0
$$
in $D(\Mod_{\Lambda_Z})$. This is the property denoted $\operatorname{BoundaryVanishing}(\Lambda,r,c)$ in the recorded Lean declaration; $\Lambda$ is exactly its sheafified constant ring $(\operatorname{finiteProperCoefficientRing} A).X$.

proof.text: Choose $n$ as in the hypothesis. For every $x\in A$, $\ell^n x=(\ell^n1_A)x=0$, so the coefficient ring is killed by a power of $\ell$, including when $A$ is the zero ring and $n=0$. By [def-pc-fibre-product], the chosen projections satisfy $r\circ a=c\circ r_Z$ and exhibit $T$ as the pullback. Use this square with $g=c$, $g'=a$, $p=r$, and $p'=r_Z$.

source.place: Proof (3), finite-coefficient proper-base-change and zero-object calculation

proof.text:
Apply clause (2) of [det-thm-sfb-proper-base-change-finite] to this square and $K$. Its proper morphism $r$ is between separated finite-type $k$-schemes; $A$ is finite and killed by a power of $\ell$ by step 1, and $K$ belongs to $\Dctf(W,\Lambda)$. Clause (2) allows arbitrary $g=c$; it requires no standing-scheme hypothesis on the new base $Z$. The canonical exchange is therefore invertible:
$$\beta_K:Lc^*Rr_*K\xrightarrow{\sim}R(r_Z)_*La^*K.$$
The exchange meant here is precisely the unit-square-counit mate of [def-sfb-finite-proper-exchange], in the internal module categories for the sheafified constant coefficient ring. The functors are the total derived composites of [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull], so no switch to derived abelian sheaves or a different coefficient model occurs. The extra general bounded-constructibility hypothesis is retained but is not needed for this application.

source.place: Proof (3), finite-coefficient proper-base-change and zero-object calculation

proof.text:
Set $N=La^*K$, which is zero by hypothesis. Apply [def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull-adjunction] to $r_Z:T\to Z$. For every $M\in D(\Mod_{\Lambda_Z})$ its adjunction gives
$$\operatorname{Hom}(M,R(r_Z)_*N)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(Lr_Z^*M,N).$$
The right side is a singleton since $N$ is zero. Taking $M=R(r_Z)_*N$ gives $\mathrm{id}=0$ on that object. Every map into or out of it is consequently zero, by composition with its identity; hence it is a zero object. Conjugating its zero identity by the isomorphism $\beta_K$ of step 2 gives zero identity on $Lc^*Rr_*K$, proving the claimed vanishing.

It adds no new nodes and is not a re-split. Statement: I checked it hypothesis by hypothesis against the Lean definition BoundaryVanishing (ProperOpenBoundaryZero.lean:87-95) and the theorem boundaryVanishing_finite (lines 499-511). The matches are: A finite and killed by ell^n with n=0 allowed; char k a prime p different from ell; W and Ybar separated of finite type over k; r a proper k-morphism; Z and c arbitrary; K a constant-model Dctf object that is also bounded constructible; a the first projection of W x_Ybar Z. The coefficient Lambda is the sheafified constant ring finiteProperCoefficientRing A, and the pushforward and pullback are the total derived composites (CondensedModuleDerivedPushpull.lean:40-57). Edge cases A=0, K=0, empty Z or T, and c=id all hold. Step 1 builds the cartesian square from def-pc-fibre-product and checks the ell-power annihilation; it is elementary and correct. Step 2 uses clause (2) of det-thm-sfb-proper-base-change-finite. Its statement puts no condition on the new base Y', its proof step 4 says no qcqs assumption is imposed on X' or Y', and its Lean finiteProperBaseChange (lines 620-636) quantifies over arbitrary schemes X', Y' with the same coefficient and input class. So taking c arbitrary is legitimate, and the exchange is the unit-square-counit mate (def-sfb-finite-proper-exchange) in the internal-module categories. Step 3: the derived adjunction holds for every morphism, so a right adjoint sends the zero object to a zero object; the step is elementary and correct. proof_deps equals the union of the uses. No duplicate exists: the parent's statement is different and the item is strictly smaller than the base-change theorem. Mathlib searches were recorded for grep, LeanSearch, LeanFinder and Loogle. Accepted tool_use: det-thm-sfb-proper-base-change-finite, used as black-box finite proper base change; the parent lem-sfb-proper-open-boundary-zero already carries this tool_use. Batch-5 flags: (1) det-thm-sfb-proper-base-change-finite is a general six-functor tool, neither the trace formula nor Poincare duality nor a step of their proofs. It reaches sec-trace-formula only through a generic derived-monoidal lemma, and the parent already cites it. (2) def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull-adjunction is a general definition. Both are genuinely outside the assumed statements, so I accepted them. No fixes were written.
